newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won ends at 880, further dollar climbs seen.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won ends at 880, further dollar climbs seen.

text.p: The won closed Monday's trading at 880.00, the level at which the central Bank of Korea (BOK) has committed to limiting the dollar's rise, dealers said.
A steady inflow of importer settlements pushed the won to fall to a low of 881.50, forcing the central bank to step into the market to sell dollars, traders added.
The won had opened the day at 879.80, compared to last Friday's close of 879.30.
"The BOK doesn't want 880 broken. But the dollar is on an uptrend because there is no other choice," said a European dealer.

The central bank was also seen offering to sell dollars in the forward market earlier in the day. It offered to sell $30 million each at 893.00 in three-month forward trading, and at 907.00 in six-month forward trading.
The bank refused to comment on talk of its intervention on the interbank market.
"If the BOK comes in tomorrow, the dollar/won could stay in a tight 879-880 range. But if it doesn't, it could move between 880-885," predicted a local bank dealer.
